text: List view: vim-style aim cursor over the flat list of visible rows
description: Audit finding (2026-09-28). Aim navigation is not vim-like: j never descends into an expanded aim's children (navigateDown ignores expansion; its dontDescend param is unused), while k descends into an expanded previous sibling only if a stale selectedIncomingIndex is set, so j and k are not inverses. Cursor state is scattered: phase.selectedAimIndex lives on data-store Phase entities, floatingAimIndex separately, and nested AimUIState.selectedIncomingIndex chains encode the sub-aim path. Target: derive the visible rows of the active column (phase aims / floating aims, recursively through expanded aims) as a flat list of {aimId, path}; the cursor is one row key; j/k = ±1 row (crossing into neighbouring phases at the ends as today), h = collapse or go to parent, l = expand or step into first child, Esc leaves aim mode, J/K reorder, L/H indent/outdent. Remove navigateDown/navigateUp/goToLastChildAim index juggling and UI fields on entities. Update e2e/navigation.spec l/h test (currently encodes the non-vim behaviour).
